subject: Oxbridge Health — Integration follow-up: SDK, auth, routing & prompt governance
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@oxbridgehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@oxbridgehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo questions + next steps for integration

Hi Laura —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. We appreciated the walkthrough and wanted to capture the outstanding technical questions so we can move toward an architecture call next week. High-level items from our side: 

- SDKs: We primarily build in Node and Python. Do you have a recommended SDK for streaming and structured output/tool calling?
- Auth & keys: We're sensitive about key rotation and want to avoid long-lived API keys in app servers. What are the supported auth flows (mTLS, short-lived tokens, OIDC)?
- Routing & regions: Can requests be pinned to a US region and fail over to another region without dropping context?
- Structured output & tool calling: We want consistent JSON schemas from the model and safe tool invocation. Does Redwood provide helper libraries or validators?
- Embeddings + reranker: For clinical search & retrieval-augmented generation we’ll likely do embeddings + a reranker. Any recommendations on embedding dimension, caching, and reranker architecture?

Also attaching our initial security questionnaire and a quick PII list so you see constraints. Can we lock in an architecture review (45m) with one of your engineers next week?

Appreciate it —
Samir
Head of Product
Oxbridge Health

Attachments: Oxbridge_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf, PII_requirements.xlsx

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@oxbridgehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@oxbridgehealth.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-18T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions + next steps for integration

Hi Samir —

Great questions and thanks for sending the questionnaire — that makes things concrete. Quick answers inline and a proposed next steps list below.

SDKs: We have first-class SDKs for Node and Python that support streaming, structured output parsing, and tool-calling helpers. For structured output we provide a small schema-validator in the SDK that can automatically retry or reject responses that don't match your JSON schema. Example install: npm install @redwood/inference && pip install redwood-inference.

Auth & key rotation: Supported options:
- Short-lived bearer tokens via our token endpoint (recommended for app servers)
- OIDC integration for service accounts + automated rotation
- mTLS for private deployments (on-prem / VPC)
We discourage long-lived API keys in client-side code — prefer token exchange.

Routing & regions: You can pin routes by policy (region, latency, cost). We support automatic failover with session affinity (KV prefix caching) so you won't lose model context when failing over. We'll share a YAML snippet in the tech brief.

Structured output & tool calling: SDK helpers include schema validation, call-safe wrappers, and a tool registry pattern that ensures only allowed tools are invoked. For additional safety we recommend an instruction-wrapper (system prompt) + model-level verification step before executing critical tools.

Embeddings + reranker: Typical pattern we recommend:
- Use 1536-d embeddings (or 1024 if using smaller models) cached and sharded by namespace.
- Dense retrieval for recall + supervised reranker (small cross-encoder) for precision on the top 50 candidates.
- Batch embedding upserts and enable prefix caching to reduce token costs.

Prompt governance & injection mitigations:
- Versioned prompt repo (Git + protected branches) with a changelog and rollbacks.
- System prompt locking for production routes (admin-only changes).
- Input sanitization layers, instruction-wrappers, and a pre-execution safety check (heuristics + model-assisted red-team checks).
- Quarterly red-team cycles; we can share a starter checklist.

Next steps proposed:
1) I’ll drop a short tech brief with examples (SDK snippets, routing YAML, prompt governance checklist).
2) Book a 45m architecture call with Marcus (serving/runtime) and Neha (solutions) — please share 2 windows next week.
3) We’ll provide an eval dataset template and a sample reranker recipe for a small POC.
4) We’ll scope a preliminary cost estimate once we see throughput requirements.

Attaching a short integration brief that covers the bits above. Let us know your availability and any additional security artifacts you need.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: LA-Redwood-Integration-Brief.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@oxbridgehealth.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo questions + next steps for integration

Hi Samir / team —

I’ll be on the architecture call and wanted to add a few concrete notes that will help the POC: 

1) SDK & streaming: Use the streaming client with delta events for partial outputs; that reduces perceived latency for clinical conversational flows. Example pattern: open connection, send context, stream tokens, and on schema-mismatch raise a retry with a tighter parsing prompt.

2) Auth & rotation: If you have an internal token exchange service we recommend short-lived tokens (5–15m) issued to backend services. For private deployments we can enable mTLS and SCIM for SSO provisioning.

3) Routing policy example (YAML):
route_policy:
  - name: oxbridge-primary
    region: us-west-2
    fallbacks: [us-east-1]
    affinity: session
    model_variants: [gptx-2.7b-quant, gptx-4-onnx]

4) Embeddings & reranker: Start with 1536-d embeddings stored in a namespaced vector index (daily upserts). Use a light cross-encoder reranker trained on a small labeled set (50–200 examples) to improve top-k precision. For throughput: enable batching (128 queries per batch) and auto-batching to keep token costs down.

5) Prompt governance: We operate a Git-backed prompt repo (protected branches) with CI hooks that run prompt-unit tests (sanity prompts, injection fuzzing). For high-risk routes we recommend additional model-constraint layers (e.g., constrained decoding, allow-lists).

I’ll bring a short demo of the reranker flow on the call. Proposed times: Tue 2026-07-21 10:00–10:45 PT or Wed 2026-07-22 08:30–09:15 PT. Which works?

Thanks,
Marcus
Engineering Lead, Serving
Redwood Inference
